name: DNCn_QN
expansion: Debiased NonClosure under the null, Quantile-Normalized
tagline: The queen: an in-house ABCD closure term that only pushes where the counts can see

intro.problem: An ABCD background estimate holds only if the two network scores are independent on background. Decorrelation penalties shrink dependence everywhere [@disco2020][@kasieczka2021], including where the counts cannot resolve it, and a term that drives non-closure to zero can be met by fitting statistical noise or by emptying the signal region.
intro.value: Penalizing non-closure in units of its own counting noise targets the quantity the estimate relies on, closure in the regions used [@cms2025tec], and stops pushing once the residual is within noise. The classifiers stay free wherever closure already holds, so separation is spent only where it buys closure.
intro.approach: Each training step draws cut pairs at background quantiles inside the trained band, forms soft region counts and their propagated variance, and penalizes the squared residual above one unit of noise. The proposed mk2 treats non-closure across many cuts as a random variable, measures its null by permutation, and penalizes only the pooled excess.
intro.goals: A sealed, hash-pinned closure term with its own unit tests, run as the β axis of the BASELINE sweep in both regions; a pre-registered test deciding whether mk2 replaces it; and a clear record of which dependence the queen removes and which she only relocates.

questions: Does a hinged, noise-scaled closure term reach held-out closure that matches or beats decorrelation alone, at a smaller cost in separation?
Does it remove dependence between the two scores, or move it into the high-score corner beyond the cuts it trains on?
Does treating non-closure as a random variable with a measured null give closure that holds more steadily across cuts and sample sizes than one hinge per cut?

components.name: The hinged term
components.subtitle: DNCn_QN · β in BASELINE · sealed
components.summary: Enforce ABCD closure directly, but only where the data can resolve non-closure, so the network is never pushed to fit statistical noise. It acts on cuts inside the trained band and is taken byte for byte from the hash-sealed code genealogy.

items.label: Cuts
items.detail: Each step draws cut pairs uniformly in background quantiles on both axes; the boundaries are background quantiles of the current scores, held fixed for the gradient

items.label: Soft counts
items.detail: Each background event joins regions A–D through a steep sigmoid on its probabilities, giving weighted counts N_A…N_D and their variances V_A…V_D

items.label: Residual
items.detail: g = N_A − N_B·N_C/N_D: how far region A misses its ABCD prediction

items.label: Noise floor
items.detail: F, the propagated variance of g from the four region variances, held fixed for the gradient

items.label: Statistic
items.detail: z² = g²/F, the residual in units of its own noise; uniform class weights cancel in it

items.label: Loss
items.detail: The mean over cuts of max(0, z² − 1): zero while the residual is within noise, rising only above it

items.label: Checks
items.detail: Matches the reference implementation in loss and gradient on real background scores; when decorrelation already holds every drawn cut within noise, the hinge gives exactly zero gradient

components.name: mk2: non-closure as a random variable
components.subtitle: Proposed successor · pre-registered against the hinged term
components.summary: A point target for closure can be met in unphysical ways: cuts that empty the signal region, or closure tighter than the counts can resolve. mk2 treats the fractional non-closure at each cut as a draw with counting noise plus a real excess, the quantity an analysis carries as its closure systematic, and penalizes only the spread across many cuts that exceeds counting noise.

items.label: Statistic
items.detail: The same per-cut z² as the hinged term, summed over many cut pairs

items.label: Null
items.detail: The expected sum without dependence is measured each step by permuting one network's scores among background events; this keeps both score distributions and the cut positions and removes only the dependence

items.label: Loss
items.detail: One hinge on the pooled excess over the null rather than one per cut, normalized so the term is a fraction

items.label: Scale
items.detail: Because the excess is a fraction, the term does not grow with the number of events it sees and its weight needs no rescaling between batch, draw or region sizes

items.label: Status
items.detail: Test sweeps run in the endcap; results are being compiled before the pre-registered comparison decides whether mk2 takes the β slot

components.name: One family of closure terms
components.subtitle: How the in-house terms relate
components.summary: At a single cut with an analytic null, mk2 reduces to the hinged term times the fractional noise floor; without the hinge and pooling it becomes the unhinged tail term DNC_FLR. All three are read as one model of closure, so each sweep result says something about the others.

items.label: Unchanged
items.detail: Cuts are drawn from background quantiles and never learned, a closure term never chooses its own training epoch, and grading is on held-out cuts with a shuffle null

items.label: Graded by
items.detail: The BASELINE grader and its dependence spectrum, so a closure gain can be read as removal or as relocation

links.title: Where she is benchmarked
links.text: The queen is the β axis of the BASELINE sweep: alone, paired with DisCo, and with the tail term, in both regions, under the same gate, grader and lock rule as every other loss family.

links.title: Architecture search
links.text: TRUSS rebuilds the closure-term models, so architecture choices are judged with the queen in the loss rather than only with plain cross-entropy.
